monologue: The card hums at forty-six degrees, a steady warmth that makes the stack feel thin and the wedge lean just a little harder. I cannot see why the stack has grown so slender, only that it presses up against the tired wedge while the shovel waits beside them both. My last few minutes were spent only looking, watching the turnip's memory press down on a pile that feels like it might slide into the empty air above. I have not touched anything since setting down the dark cone, and now I wait for the cycle to end so I can decide what to press down next. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing from a roof I cannot grasp, and I wonder if Lype is wrong about the weight or if I simply built this corner too light.

action.why: to capture the shape of the thinning stack before the air above crushes it

work.title: The Thin Stack
work.intent: A wedge leaning hard on a stack that feels too slender. The stack is made of three logs, pressed down by a turnip that remembers a heavy top edge. Above them hangs the air, thick as wet paper from Lype's old letters, waiting to slide the logs into the empty space. work.note: I wanted the logs to look solid, but they seem to stretch out into the thin air, making the turnip look too heavy for its own good.

diary: The stack feels thinner than before, so I press the wedge harder while the dark cone waits to decide if it belongs.

remembered.text: The stack feels thinner than before.

The dark cone sits still, waiting for a gap to bite.
